thread:
Alex P: starting handoff — noticed a burst of 5xxs on inference-prod around 22:02 UTC. I muted noisy infra alerts but kept SLO error-rate paging on. leaving this for night team.
IncidentBot: [ALERT] inference-prod error_rate > 3% for 5m — paging @oncall (primary). Incident ID: INC-2026-331.
Alex P: quick context: we rolled a model rollback at 21:45 in us-west to fix memory regressions. traffic spike + retry storms seem to have exposed a fallback path that returns 503.
Tina L: thanks Alex. are customers impacted? any region-level outage?
Alex P: partial. about ~6% of requests in us-west saw 503s for ~6 minutes, mainly long prompts (>= 6k tokens). latency SLOs tripped for a subset. no billing/customer-facing outage reported yet.
Mike R: I'm primary for the next 2h. tagging Tina as secondary. I'm taking ownership of mitigation.
Priya (SRE Lead): plan: 1) temporarily relax non-critical error-rate paging threshold to 5% for 30m while we stabilize; 2) enable KV-cache-bypass on the affected runtime as a mitigation; 3) watch customer-facing 5xxs and escalate if > 5% persists.
Jess C: can you post the exact command for the threshold change? want to document in runbook.
Mike R: running the threshold change now: 
```
# Adjust alert policy: inference-prod/error_rate
redwoodctl alerts update --policy inference-prod/error_rate --threshold 0.05 --window 300 --note "temp raise during handoff & rollback storm" --expires-in 30m
```
Mike R: done. Alert policy update accepted, policy_id=ap-83421. IncidentBot: policy change logged.
IncidentBot: [AUDIT] alerts policy ap-83421 modified by Mike R at 22:08 UTC (temp threshold=5%, expires=30m).
Tina L: added runbook pointer in thread — https://redwood.inc/runbooks/inference-error-rate (section: transient-rollbacks). also added a quick mitigation checklist.
Alex P: good. also FYI, the fallback code path that returns 503 is in runtime v2.3.1 — engineering working on patch to avoid immediate 503s and instead queue.
Priya (SRE Lead): keep an eye on overall token throughput. if latency SLOs stay >10% above target after 15m of mitigation, we switch to model-variant fallback routing to lower-capacity model.
Jess C: documenting primary/secondary for tonight: Mike R (primary), Tina L (secondary). handoff ETA for next oncall is 00:00 UTC.
Mike R: monitoring. ping me if you see error_rate > 5% or customer complaints. I'll revert policy earlier if stable. :thumbsup:
Tina L: confirmed. I'll run a quick synthetic test set against us-west to validate the rollback path in ~10m.
Alex P: thanks team — leaving a note to add to post-incident: "consider making alert suppression window configurable per-route" if this pattern recurs.
IncidentBot: [NOTE] This thread will be linked to INC-2026-331. Remember to fill in incident impact and RCA after resolution.
Mike R: closing loop for now — mitigation active, threshold temporary, runbook linked. last check-in 22:15 UTC.
Tina L: 22:30 update: synthetic checks look stable, error_rate down to 1.2% in us-west, reverting mute on infra alerts.
Mike R: will schedule policy revert at 22:38 UTC (30m expiry). if anything spikes before then I will revert earlier.
Priya (SRE Lead): nice work. will follow up with postmortem if we end up doing rollback patch.
Alex P: handing off to night team — passing primary to Mike R. good luck.
